evidence_summary: Mid r0 cost rankings are not uniform across countries: CHL/MEX have GMI ideal as the lowest gross cost, while PER/COL have PEN as the lowest; no mid r0 cell crosses. The expected broad cost gradient toward high-cost UBI is visible, but PEN/MUT/GMI ordering is country- and version-dependent.
notes: Preliminary: final ranking claims must keep GMI ideal and loaded together and should not infer an operational ranking from ideal GMI alone.

statement: Preparedness/adoption matter more than total exposure across countries
evidence_summary: Official baseline uses common LAC fallback E_prod for all four countries, so between-country variation in T is mechanically driven by preparedness, adoption, informality, and Gap rather than measured country-specific exposure.
notes: Not testable in the cross-country exposure margin until country-specific E_prod is available.

statement: High informality reduces feasibility through adoption and fiscal channels
evidence_summary: The official grid contains the two channels, but no adoption-only/fiscal-only ablation has been run in Phase A. Directional evidence is consistent with lower adoption ceilings in higher-informality settings, but causal channel separation is pending diagnostics.
notes: Requires Tier D ablations before confirmatory adjudication.

evidence_summary: At xi=0.10, mid has no crossings under any regime, but stress crossings remain three cells while V>=1.10 crossings rise from 2 in r0 to 3 in r2/r4; r4 materially raises V for CHL GMI and PER PEN.
notes: Preliminary deterministic evidence; companion erosion is present for r>=1.

statement: Crossings requiring historically extreme fiscal capture are fragile
evidence_summary: Official xi=0.10 crossings are all classified fiscally_ordinary against total revenue; no crossing with extreme_or_outside_historical_support is present. No violation of the fragile-extreme rule is observed.
notes: Preliminary: positive stress-test evidence requires a cell with extreme capture or a targeted synthetic check.
